entities.summary: Vince Nagy de Losonc was a Hungarian politician, who served as Interior Minister between 1918 and 1919 during the Hungarian Democratic Republic. After the establishment of the Hungarian Soviet Republic, he returned to Szatmárnémeti, where the occupying Romanian Army imprisoned him for 9 months. From 1922, he was a lawyer. From 1928, he was the chairman of the Independence Party. After the German occupation Nagy had to escape because of his anti-Nazi views. After the Second World War, he rejected the cooperation with the Hungarian Communist Party and so he was excluded, along with 18 other members from the party.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Interior Minister of the Hungarian Democratic Republic from 1918 to 1919, Vince Nagy played a key role in shaping the country's early 20th-century politics. His subsequent exclusion from the Hungarian Communist Party following World War II had limited regional impact.
